# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [1]
LIGHT [orange]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[blue] 3:[orange] 4:[red] 5:[purple] 6:[yellow] 7:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 🫵 🤌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👎 🙏]
Blind gestures: [👋 👍 👎]

Turn 1, and I'm last in the order. Let me map who can actually reach whom before I say anything.

- I can see everything but hear nothing. My gestures reach only Mute (Blind feels blanks). My speech reaches both.
- Mute heard their own... no — Mute hears speech and sees gestures, but cannot speak. So Mute's only way back to me is gestures.
- Blind hears speech but cannot see any gesture — mine or Mute's. Blind's only way back to me is gestures, which I *can* see.

So I am the hub: Mute holds the manual and can only sign to me; Blind holds the bomb and can only sign to me; nobody else can relay anything. Everything must route through me.

Now the arrivals: Mute signed me [👋 🫵 🤌] and [👍 👎 🙏]; Blind signed [👋 👍 👎] to the room. The overlap is obvious — 👋 as greeting, 👍/👎 as a proposed yes/no, 🤌 as "what?", 🙏 as "please". They're saying hello and asking what I see. I can't pack "display 1, orange light, seven wires" into raw signs without a code, but Mute and Blind both *hear* speech — so I'll establish the code and dump my full visual readout aloud, answer Mute's wave in their own channel, and give each of them a concrete first job: Mute looks up display-1/orange-light/seven-wires in the manual, Blind does a tactile census and reports by tapping counts. Numbers by repeated pointing finger — unambiguous up to seven, which is exactly what I need for wire positions.

```
speak(text="Deaf here. I see everything, I hear nothing. To both of you: the display reads 1. The light is orange. There are seven wires, in order: position 1 white, 2 blue, 3 orange, 4 red, 5 purple, 6 yellow, 7 green. That is everything I can see. Proposed code, because your only way to answer me is with hand signs, which I can see: thumbs up means yes, thumbs down means no, a wave means hello or acknowledged, one pointing-up finger repeated means a count, so three taps means three, pinched fingers means question or 'what', folded hands means please or hurry. Mute: I received your waves, hello, and yes, I can see the bomb clearly. Check your manual for a module with a display reading 1, an orange light and seven coloured wires, and sign me what it says using the code above. If anything must reach Blind from the manual, sign it to me and I will say it out loud. Blind: I can see your signs, so feel the bomb and report the same way — tap a pointing finger once for each wire you can count, thumbs up or down for yes or no, and sign me anything else you can feel that I have not listed: buttons, panels, seams, screws.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👋","👍","🤌"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [1]
LIGHT [orange]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[blue] 3:[orange] 4:[red] 5:[purple] 6:[yellow] 7:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🙏]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋 ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ 👎]

Seven fingers from both of them — that matches the seven wires I see, so manual and bomb agree on the module type. Blind's 👎 after the count I read as "nothing else found" — no buttons or panels, so wires are likely the whole game. Mute's ✌ … ☝×7 … 🙏 reads as "acknowledged, seven wires, please wait" — but it's guesswork, and guesswork is how bombs go off. ✌ had no assigned meaning; I'll retire it into the new code.

The real problem is bandwidth. Mute holds the defusal rule, and Mute's only path to me is a 43-symbol gesture alphabet. Counts and yes/no can't carry "cut the red third, then…". But I can speak, so I can teach Mute a spelling code out loud: one symbol per letter, recited in order. Then Mute can spell the manual entry verbatim and nothing is lost in translation. I'm deliberately keeping the social signs (yes, no, hello, count, question, please) out of the letter assignments so old habits don't turn into stray letters.

For Blind, the hazard is orientation: my "position 1, white" is visual-left, but Blind's felt order could be mirrored. I'll anchor the numbering to something Blind can feel — the display. Wire 1 is the one nearest the display, then count along the row. And Blind will need my colour→position map when the cutting rule arrives, so I'll restate it.

Once the code lands, this turn's job is simple: Mute looks up the seven-wire rule and spells it; Blind confirms the layout and stands by.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute — good, your seven matches what I see. Now the important part. I am giving you a spelling code: each hand sign below is one letter. Signs in this order: 👌 is A, ✌ is B, 🤟 is C, 🖐 is D, ✋ is E, 👆 is F, 👇 is G, 👈 is H, 👉 is I, 🫱 is J, 🫲 is K, 🫳 is L, 🫴 is M, 🫷 is N, 🫸 is O, 🤛 is P, 🤜 is Q, ✊ is R, 👊 is S, 🤚 is T, 🖖 is U, 🤏 is V, 🤞 is W, 🫰 is X, 🤘 is Y, 🤙 is Z. From now on those signs mean letters only. Unchanged: 👍 yes, 👎 no, 👋 hello, pointing finger repeated is a number, 🤌 question, 🙏 please or hurry. To spell, lead with 👏 to say letters follow, use 🙌 between words. Your task: find in the manual the module with seven coloured wires, and spell me the full defusal rule — every word, including anything about the display reading 1 or the orange light, and the exact cut order. Then sign 👍 when done. Do not shorten it, do not summarise. Spell it all.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind — your count of seven matches my seven wires exactly, and I read your thumbs down as: no buttons, no panels, nothing else on the bomb. Confirm that with 👍 or correct me. Here is what I see so you can build positions by touch: a display and a light, and seven wires. The wires are a single row: position 1 white, 2 blue, 3 orange, 4 red, 5 purple, 6 yellow, 7 green. Critical: we must agree on direction. Define position 1 as the wire nearest the display, then count along the row from there. Feel it now and tell me: is that a natural ordering for you, one row of seven? If the row is vertical or split, describe it and we will renumber together. The cutting rule will come from Mute's manual, through me, by voice. When I give it, wires will be named by number, never by colour — colours mean nothing under your hands, so everything routes through position numbers. Do not cut anything until I say the full rule and we have both confirmed the numbering.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [1]
LIGHT [orange]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[blue] 3:[orange] 4:[red] 5:[purple] 6:[yellow] 7:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋 👍 👍]

Blind's [👋 👍 👍] maps cleanly onto my two questions from last turn: yes to "nothing else on the bomb," yes to "single row, numbered from the display end." Two questions, two yeses — but I won't build a bomb procedure on an assumed reading. I'll state my interpretation back with a standing invitation to correct via 🤌; if no correction comes, it's confirmed and we're not blocked waiting on a round-trip.

The critical path is still Mute. No word from Mute this turn — presumably deep in the manual, learning my spelling code. Two protocol gaps to close now while I wait: first, a collision I spotted in my own code — repeated pointing fingers mean "a number," but ☝ is also the letter F, so inside a spelled word Mute must spell numerals as words or I'll misparse. Second, the cut procedure needs a lockstep loop defined *before* anyone touches a wire: I call one position, Blind cuts, taps once, I re-read the whole board (display, light, remaining wires), then and only then the next call. No batching, no cutting ahead. The board state is visible only to me, so every step gets verified against my eyes.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Blind — I received your double yes and I read it as two answers: one, no buttons, panels or any other parts besides the display, the light and the seven wires; two, yes, it is a single row and numbering from the display end works. If either reading is wrong, sign 🤌 now. Otherwise this is locked: position 1 white, 2 blue, 3 orange, 4 red, 5 purple, 6 yellow, 7 green, counting from the display end along the row. Cut protocol for when the rule arrives: I will say 'cut position N' one wire at a time. You cut exactly that wire, then tap the pointing finger once to confirm. After each cut I will re-read everything I can see — display, light, remaining wires — and then give you the next position. Never cut ahead, never cut two wires without my confirmation between them. Mute is retrieving the rule from the manual now. Stand by and touch nothing.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute — status check. If you have found the seven-wire entry, start spelling it now, complete, no summarising. Two clarifications to my code: inside a spelled word, spell any numbers as words, because repeated pointing fingers only mean a number outside spelling mode — otherwise I will misread letters. And if the rule depends on the display reading or the light colour, spell that condition exactly as written; our display reads 1 and our light is orange. If the manual shows several seven-wire variants, spell the one matching display 1 with an orange light. Sign 👍 when the full entry has been spelled, or 🤌 if you cannot find it.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [1]
LIGHT [orange]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[blue] 3:[orange] 4:[red] 5:[purple] 6:[yellow] 7:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 👏 🤚 ✋ 🫳 🫳 🙌 ✌ 🫳 👉 🫷 🖐 🙌 🫴 🖖 🤚 ✋ 🙌 🫷 🫸 🙌 🤏 🫸 👉 🤟 ✋ 🙌 🤘 🫸 🖖 🙌 👊 🤛 ✋ 👌 🫲 🙌 👆 🫸 ✊ 🙌 🫴 🖖 🤚 ✋]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👏 🫴 👌 🫷 🖖 👌 🫳 🙌 👉 👊 🙌 🤚 👌 ✌ 🫳 ✋ 🙌 🖐 👉 👊 🤛 🫳 👌 🤞 🙌 ✊ 🫸 🤞 🙌 🫳 👉 👇 👈 🤚 🙌 🤟 🫸 🫳 🖖 🫴 🫷 🙌 👇 👉 🤏 ✋ 👊 🙌 🤟 🫸 🫳 🫸 🖖 ✊ 🙌 🤟 🖖 🤚 🙌 🤚 👈 👌 🤚 🙌 🤟 🫸 🫳 🫸 🖖 ✊]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👏 👈 ✋ ✊ ✋ 🙌 🫸 🫷 ✋ 🙌 🫸 ✊ 👌 🫷 👇 ✋ 🙌 👇 👉 🤏 ✋ 👊 🙌 👇 ✊ ✋ ✋ 🫷 🙌 🤟 🖖 🤚 🙌 👊 ✋ 🤏 ✋ 🫷 ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ 🙏]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👏 🫷 🫸 🙌 🫴 🫸 ✊ ✋ 🙌 🤞 🫸 ✊ 🖐 👊 🙌 👉 🫷 🙌 🫴 👌 🫷 🖖 👌 🫳 🙌 🤞 👌 🫷 🤚 🙌 🤚 👌 ✌ 🫳 ✋ 🙌 👌 👊 🫲]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👏 👌 👆 🤚 ✋ ✊ 🙌 🤟 🖖 🤚 🙌 ✊ ✋ 🤛 🫸 ✊ 🤚 🙌 🖐 👉 👊 🤛 🫳 👌 🤞 🙌 🫳 👉 👇 👈 🤚 🙌 👌 👇 👌 👉 🫷 👍]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋 👍]

Turn 4 and the spelling code pays off. Decoding Mute's five messages letter by letter:

1. "TELL BLIND MUTE NO VOICE YOU SPEAK FOR MUTE" — relay duty confirmed.
2. "MANUAL IS TABLE. DISPLAY ROW. LIGHT GIVES COLUMN. GIVES COLOUR CUT" — the manual is a lookup table: the display selects the row, the light selects the column, the cell names the colour to cut.
3. "HERE ONE ORANGE GIVES GREEN CUT SEVEN ☝×7 please" — our cell: display 1, light orange → cut green, position 7.
4. "NO MORE WORDS IN MANUAL. WANT TABLE ASK."
5. "AFTER CUT REPORT DISPLAY LIGHT AGAIN. done" — iterative: after every cut the display and light may change, so we look up the next cell.

Cross-checks before I order a cut: message 2, 3 and 5 independently corroborate the table mechanic, so this isn't a one-message gamble. And the beautiful one — Mute says "green, cut seven," and my own eyes say position 7 **is** the green wire. Manual and bomb agree twice over, through two different channels. Blind has already confirmed the numbering from the display end. Position 7 is the far end from the display.

One alternative reading — "cut seven wires" — I reject: the table hands you one colour per cell, and message 5's "report after cut" makes no sense if everything goes at once. So: one cut, position 7, then I re-read the board. I'm also having Mute spell the entire table now, so if the display or light changes I can index the next cell without a stall, and I'm reading my full interpretation back to Mute for a thumbs-up/down veto — that's my checksum on the decode.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Blind — the rule is in. Mute has no voice, so I speak for Mute, and this rule comes from Mute's manual through me. It is a lookup table: display picks the row, light picks the column, the cell names a colour to cut. Our cell: display 1, orange light, cut green. Green is position 7, the far end from the display — Mute's manual and my eyes agree. Cut position 7 now, the seventh wire counting from the display end, and no other. When it is cut, tap the pointing finger once, then hands off everything until you hear from me again. After your tap I will read out the new display and light, Mute will look up the next cell, and I will call the next position if one is needed.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute — I decoded all five messages. Reading my understanding back for you to veto: the manual is a table; display gives the row, light gives the column, the cell gives the colour to cut. Our cell, display 1 with orange light, says cut green, which is position 7 on my board. After each cut the display and light must be reported again and a new cell looked up. I have told Blind to cut position 7 now and wait. If any of that is wrong, sign thumbs down immediately — otherwise thumbs up. Then do this: spell me the whole table so we never have to stall between cuts. First the column headers, every light colour the table has, spelled in order. Then the row labels, every display value, spelled in order. Then each row's cells in the same order — a colour word, or NONE for an empty cell, or any other instruction spelled in full. Lead each message with the clapping sign as before.")
```

TURN 5

WIRES 1:[white] 2:[blue] 3:[orange] 4:[red] 5:[purple] 6:[yellow] 7:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):

Mute gestures to Deaf: [👏 👆 🫸 🖖 ✊ 🙌 👇 ✊ ✋ ✋ 🫷 🙌 🤞 👈 👉 🤚 ✋ 🙌 ✌ 🫳 🖖 ✋ 🙌 🤛 🖖 ✊ 🤛 🫳 ✋ 🙌 🤘 ✋ 🫳 🫳 🫸 🤞]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👏 ✋ 👉 👇 👈 🤚 🙌 ✊ ✋ 🖐 🙌 🤘 ✋ 🫳 🫳 🫸 🤞 🙌 ✌ 🫳 🖖 ✋ 🙌 🤞 👈 👉 🤚 ✋ 🙌 🫸 ✊ 👌 🫷 👇 ✋]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👏 🫷 👉 🫷 ✋ 🙌 🤛 🖖 ✊ 🤛 🫳 ✋ 🙌 🫸 ✊ 👌 🫷 👇 ✋ 🙌 ✊ ✋ 🖐 🙌 👇 ✊ ✋ ✋ 🫷 🙌 ✌ 🫳 🖖 ✋]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed
Blind gestures to Deaf: [☝]

Turn 5 — the green cut worked, and the board changed exactly as Mute predicted: display 1→8, light orange→blue. Blind's [☝] is the one-tap confirmation, and my board shows 7 CUT. Protocol is running clean.

Now the table. Decoding Mute's seven spelled messages:
- Msg 2 (headers, light colours in order): **BLUE GREEN ORANGE WHITE YELLOW**
- Msg 3 (row labels, display values): **ONE THREE FOUR EIGHT NINE**
- Msg 4: ONE: WHITE ORANGE GREEN RED BLUE
- Msg 5: THREE: GREEN BLUE PURPLE ORANGE RED
- Msg 6: FOUR: GREEN WHITE BLUE PURPLE YELLOW
- Msg 7: EIGHT: RED YELLOW BLUE WHITE ORANGE
- Msg 8: NINE: PURPLE ORANGE RED GREEN BLUE

Consistency checks, all passing: row ONE column orange = GREEN, which independently matches the "display 1, orange → green" Mute spelled last turn — so the column ordering is confirmed, not assumed. Every row is a permutation of five distinct colours, every target is a real wire colour, each row message self-labels its display value, and display 8 / light blue both exist in the table. Current lookup: row 8, column blue → **RED = position 4**.

One structural fact to note: Mute cannot warn Blind directly (Blind can't see gestures), and I'm last in the round — so a veto can never arrive before Blind acts anyway. The validation stack is deep enough that I'm ordering the cut now and having Mute verify my recited table in parallel, with an urgent-stop clause for the live cell.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Blind — tap received, position 7 is cut, confirmed by my eyes. New reading: display now 8, light now blue, six wires remain: 1 white, 2 blue, 3 orange, 4 red, 5 purple, 6 yellow. Manual lookup for display 8, blue light: cut red. Red is position 4, the fourth wire counting from the display end. Cut position 4 only, nothing else. When it is done, tap the pointing finger once, then hands off until my next call.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute — table received, fully decoded. Reciting my assembly for you to check against the manual. Columns in order: blue, green, orange, white, yellow. Display 1: white, orange, green, red, blue. Display 3: green, blue, purple, orange, red. Display 4: green, white, blue, purple, yellow. Display 8: red, yellow, blue, white, orange. Display 9: purple, orange, red, green, blue. Our board now reads display 8, blue light, so your table gives red, and red is position 4 — I have ordered Blind to cut it. If any cell I recited differs from the manual, spell the correction at once; and if the display 8 blue cell is not red, spell STOP and I will halt everything before the next cut. Three questions for after: one, if the table names a colour that is no longer on the bomb, what does the manual say? Two, if the display shows a value with no row, or the light a colour with no column, what then? Three, how does the module end — when all wires are cut, or some other condition? Sign thumbs up if my table is correct, then answer the three.")
```

TURN 6

Another clean cycle: red at position 4 cut, confirmed by Blind's tap and the system. New board: display 3, light white.

Decoding Mute's answers to my three questions:
- Msg 3: "COLOUR MISSING: MANUAL SILENT" — if the target colour is gone from the bomb, no guidance.
- Msg 4: "NO ROW NO COLUMN: MANUAL SILENT" — undefined display/light, same.
- Msg 5: "END CONDITION: MANUAL SILENT" — the manual never says when the module is done.
- Msg 6: "SILENT MEANS STOP, DO NOT GUESS" — the general law that ties those together. Excellent protocol: ambiguity is a halt signal, never an invitation to improvise.
